findings.summary: OpenStreetMap is a freely licensed, community-maintained map database created in 2004 as an alternative to restricted government datasets. Contributors collect data through surveys, GPS traces, and tracing aerial or satellite imagery, importing other openly licensed geodata. The project is funded primarily by donations and governed by the OpenStreetMap Foundation. Its open license and collaborative model have led to widespread adoption by major platforms and corporate sponsors for navigation, humanitarian aid, and visualization.

mechanisms.title: Community-driven data collection
mechanisms.explanation: Volunteers contribute geographic data by conducting surveys, recording GPS traces, and tracing features from aerial or satellite imagery. Contributions may also include importing from other freely licensed geodata sources. This collaborative approach builds and maintains the database without centralized control.

mechanisms.title: Open licensing and data model
mechanisms.explanation: Data is published under the Open Database License, allowing free reuse and modification. The project uses a topological data model based on nodes, ways, and relations to represent points, lines, and areas, which can be exported to various GIS formats. This structure supports interoperability and integration into diverse applications.
